projectIdentity.name: aidm-pilot-task-queue
projectIdentity.purpose: A reliable prioritized in-memory task queue engine supporting FIFO/priority scheduling, task leasing, TTL expiration, deterministic state snapshots, and JSON serialization/deserialization.
projectIdentity.desiredOutcome: A small, real, independently versioned TypeScript project implementing a reliable in-memory task queue library with comprehensive automated test coverage.

inScope: Domain models: TaskItem, TaskPriority, QueueConfig, TaskLease
Queue operations: enqueue, dequeue, peek, lease, release, expireStale
Persistence representation: deterministic JSON state serialization, JSON deserialization, schema validation
Verification: unit tests, integration/E2E tests, build/typecheck verification
targetUsers: Developers and software systems requiring a prioritized in-memory task queue engine with leasing and snapshot determinism
primaryWorkflows: State Serialization and Deserialization Round-trip with Schema Validation

capabilities.title: Core Functionality
capabilities.description:
The pilot project is: aidm-pilot-task-queue
Purpose:
A reliable prioritized in-memory task queue engine supporting:
- FIFO/priority scheduling
- task leasing
- TTL expiration
- deterministic state snapshots
- JSON serialization/deserialization

The eventual pilot is intended to be a small, real, independently versioned TypeScript project.
capabilities.behavior: System executes core functional capabilities requested by Product Owner.

capabilities.title: Domain Models & Schema Validation
capabilities.description: Type definitions and schema validation for TaskItem, TaskPriority, QueueConfig, and TaskLease.
capabilities.behavior: Enforces type safety and validates input parameters when tasks and queue configurations are created.
businessRules: TaskPriority determines scheduling preference
QueueConfig specifies default lease durations, TTL limits, and queue capacities
TaskLease tracks active leases with leaseholder identity and expiration timestamp

capabilities.title: Deterministic State Serialization & Snapshots
capabilities.description: Deterministic JSON state serialization, deserialization, and schema validation of queue state snapshots.
capabilities.behavior: Serializes entire in-memory queue state to canonical JSON string and reconstructs state identically upon deserialization.
businessRules: JSON serialization must be strictly deterministic (reproducible ordering)
Deserialization validates state against schema before restoring in-memory queue

capabilities.title: Prioritized In-Memory Queue Operations
capabilities.description: Queue operations including enqueue, dequeue, peek, lease, release, and expireStale.
capabilities.behavior: Manages task transitions through queued, leased, completed, and expired states with FIFO tie-breaking within identical priority levels.
businessRules: FIFO ordering strictly enforced within the same TaskPriority level
Leased tasks are hidden from dequeue until released or expired
expireStale reclaims expired leases and evicts TTL-exceeded tasks

behaviors: Deterministic priority-based scheduling with FIFO tie-breaking
Exclusive task leasing with automatic reclamation upon expiration
businessRules: FIFO ordering preserved within identical priority levels
Leased tasks cannot be dequeued by another worker until lease expires or is released
expireStale evicts tasks exceeding TTL or resets expired leases
State snapshot JSON serialization must be deterministic and schema-validated

performance: High-throughput in-memory queue operations with low algorithmic complexity
security: No external network exposure, isolated in-memory execution, input schema validation
reliability: Deterministic state machine transitions, zero task loss during valid lease/release lifecycle
scalability: Bounded in-memory footprint suitable for embedded Node.js library usage
availability: Always available synchronously within host process
usability: Idiomatic TypeScript API with strongly typed contracts and clear error handling

architecturalConstraints: Pure in-memory engine, no external network dependencies or external daemon connections
Modular separation of domain models, queue engine, and serialization adapters
integrationRequirements: Consumable as an independent TypeScript module / library
dataStorageExpectations: In-memory data structures with deterministic JSON snapshot serialization/deserialization

expectedBehavior: End-to-end functionality of aidm-pilot-task-queue according to specified capabilities
Tasks are enqueued, dequeued, leased, released, and expired deterministically
Queue state can be serialized to JSON and deserialized without data loss or corruption
measurableCriteria: Automated test suite passing with zero regressions
100% automated test pass rate across unit and integration/E2E test suites
TypeScript compiler check passes with zero errors under strict mode
definitionOfCompletion: All functional capabilities verified by automated tests
No unresolved blocking discovery questions or pending Product Owner decisions
All in-scope domain models, queue operations, and persistence routines implemented
Automated test suite passing and verifying FIFO/priority, leasing, TTL, and serialization

technicalRisks.statement: Clock drift or non-monotonic system clock could cause unexpected lease expirations if not handled carefully
technicalRisks.mitigation: Use monotonic time or injectable clock interface for testing and lease evaluation
